title: Exploring the motivation and structural barriers of women's sports consumption from the perspective of the "She-Economy".
authors: Shi Y, Yang T, Zhang K, Yi C.
abstract: Against the backdrop of consumption upgrading and growing gender consciousness, the "She-Economy" has emerged as an important socio-economic phenomenon driving market transformation and consumption restructuring. Women's participation in sports consumption has continued to increase, making women a significant consumer group within the sports industry. However, women's sports consumption is a contradictory field in which empowerment, identity formation, market discipline, gender norms, institutional neglect, and structural inequality coexist. Therefore, this study adopted a descriptive phenomenological design and employed literature review and semi-structured in-depth interviews with nine Chinese women who had sports consumption experience. Colaizzi's seven-step method was used to conduct thematic analysis of the interview data in order to explore the motivations and structural barriers underlying women's sports consumption within the context of the "She-Economy". The findings reveal that women's sports consumption is driven by multiple motivations, including health management, social interaction, self-realization, and market-driven incentives. Sports consumption not only reflects women's pursuit of physical health and emotional well-being, but also demonstrates the growing awakening of female subjectivity and lifestyle autonomy. However, women continue to face structural constraints in the process of sports consumption, including time pressure, economic costs, gender-role expectations, male-dominated sports spaces, and insufficient institutional support. These findings reflect a paradoxical coexistence between strengthened consumption motivation and restricted behavioral practice. The findings extend current understanding of women's sports consumption under the "She-Economy" by showing that women's sports consumption is a socially negotiated practice in which individual agency and structural constraints continuously interact. The study also provides exploratory, context-specific insights into women-centered sports products and services, supportive socio-cultural environments, and more gender-responsive sports services, offering qualitative evidence for future research and practice.

title: Psychological and computational evidence that merit is a constructed evaluative process.
authors: Vahed S, Sanfey AG.
abstract: Merit is a foundational moral principle invoked to justify inequality between people, yet an individual's productivity is shaped not only by their efforts but also their opportunities. How, then, do people construct merit judgements? Across four preregistered, incentivized studies with US-based samples (total N = 759), we provide psychological and computational evidence that merit is not the product of a fixed rule, but rather the outcome of a subjective valuation. In a two-stage paradigm, participants first completed a real-effort tournament that dissociated performance (effort) from structural productivity (output dependent on opportunity). Thereafter, groups of observers and stakeholders allocated resources to tournament players. Across studies, a player's performance and structural productivity influenced how people judged deservingness. Computational modeling revealed that decision-makers integrated these dimensions of merit into a value computation that shaped allocations. Crucially, individuals differed in their latent weighting patterns, yielding subgroups with directly opposing conceptions of deservingness. By revealing merit as a nonuniform ideal, these findings provide a mechanistic account of how deservingness is determined, helping explain the compelling yet contested nature of meritocracy.

title: Obscured Rhythms: Using Rhythmanalysis to Understand How Symptoms Associated With Menopause Shape Everyday Experiences of Physical Activity.
authors: Phoenix C, Griffin M, Bennett EV.
abstract: Physical activity (PA) is frequently promoted as a means of managing symptoms associated with the menopause transition (MT), yet little is known of how the embodied, emotional and temporal disruptions of menopause influence the experiences of, and possibilities for, movement. Taking inspiration from French sociologist Henri Lefebvre's theory of 'rhythmanalysis' and Jennifer Mason's facet methodology approach, we draw on qualitative survey responses from 249 women to examine how symptoms associated with the MT interrelate with space and time to shape everyday experiences of PA. Our findings highlight how symptoms intertwine with seasonal, hormonal and circadian cycles to reconfigure everyday tempos of energy, rest and aspirations to move more. These shifting rhythms often constrain participation in PA, but also prompt creative adjustments including new pacing strategies, altered routines and re-attunements to bodily fluctuation. Our rhythmanalytic approach challenges binary framings of PA as either hindered or facilitated, offering instead a textured account of how movement, stillness and slowing are negotiated during the MT. These original insights contribute to embodied and critical perspectives on health, demonstrating the value of more flexible, rhythmic and context-sensitive approaches to promoting movement through the MT.

title: Female Representation and Quality Indicators in Anesthesiology and Critical Care Podcasts.
authors: Steinsdóttir P, Asif S, Kristinsdóttir RN, Rosenström A, Niklasson A, Dietz N, Fåhraeus SÅ, Hylander J, Bjurström MF.
abstract: Background Podcasts have emerged as prominent tools for asynchronous medical education, widely adopted across training levels and specialties. Diverse representation strengthens medical discourse, making an evaluation of speaker demographics essential for understanding equity and quality in digital knowledge dissemination. This study systematically evaluates female representation and quality assurance indicators in anesthesiology and critical care podcasts, including longitudinal publication trends. Methods We systematically searched Apple Podcasts and Spotify using specialty-specific terms and manually reviewed the top twenty journals in the field for affiliated podcasts. Included were active, English-language, physician-hosted podcasts. Results Eighty-five podcasts (53.0% US-based) comprising 10,190 episodes were analyzed. Of 12,522 hosts, 31.5% (n = 3945) were female; of 10,822 guests, 35.9% (n = 3882) were female. Notably, among US-based podcasts, female guest representation exceeded the 26.5% female workforce proportion among US anesthesiologists. Episodes with exclusively male hosts had 2.13 times the odds of featuring only male guests (95% CI 1.88-2.41). A positive trend of increasing female participation was observed from 2010 to 2024. Content support was variable: using broad, inclusive definitions, 42.0% of episodes had show notes and 48.4% provided supplemental material. Analysis of quality-related structures showed that 40.0% (n = 34) of podcasts produced episodes linked to a publication, 50.6% featured some episodes with three or more speakers, 21.2% of podcasts were journal-affiliated, and 20.0% were university-affiliated. Conclusion While a sex imbalance persists in anesthesiology and critical care podcasting, female participation among US-based podcasts exceeds local workforce demographic benchmarks, with a clear positive trend from 2010 to 2024. However, persistent sex similarity in speaker selection suggests ongoing biases. Quality assurance mechanisms remain highly variable, highlighting opportunities for incremental improvement. Future efforts could focus on structured guest selection and transparent quality indicators to accelerate progress toward equitable representation and educational quality in this influential medium. Editorial comment In modern times, many clinicians look for, and listen to, podcasts aimed at education in clinical specialties. This sampling of podcasts related to our specialty looked at how females and males contributed to podcast content generation and dissemination, as a marker for male versus female representation in speakership for continuing specialty education.

title: Exploring barriers to implementing adolescent pregnancy prevention interventions in low- and middle-income countries: Perspectives from international experts.
authors: Nkurunziza A, Nkurikiyintwali JMV, Ndayisenga JP, Kasine Y, Twagirayezu I, Uwera YDN.
abstract: Background Adolescent pregnancy remains a significant public health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Although various interventions have been implemented to address this issue, many have failed to achieve positive outcomes due to numerous barriers. Objective To explore the barriers to implementing adolescent pregnancy prevention interventions in LMICs. Methods This qualitative exploratory study involved 19 adolescent pregnancy prevention program implementers across 24 LMICs. Data were collected through virtual in-depth individual interviews, organized using Dedoose software, and analyzed thematically. Results Findings highlighted seven interrelated challenges shaping programme reach, acceptability, and sustainability. Experts reported that adolescents' engagement depended on perceived usefulness and, at times, material or social benefits of attendance, while stigma made participation social risky and encouraged private information-seeking. Prevention efforts were further constrained by gendered allocation and unequal decision-making power, which limited boys' participation and girls' agency. Separately, poverty, household material insecurity, and transactional marriage practices such as bride price contributed to early unions and subsequent childbearing, while programme legitimacy is challenged by taboo, religious opposition, contraception myths, and the normalization of violence. Finally, implementation was hindered by administrative delays, weak institutional backing, school-level resistance, and unstable or poorly enforced policy environments, limiting continuity and scale-up of interventions. Conclusion Effective teenage pregnancy prevention in LMICs requires more than delivering sexual and reproductive health (SRH) information; programmes must be designed to feel relevant to adolescents while reducing stigma and protecting confidentiality to support genuine engagement. Interventions also need to address gendered power dynamics and gatekeeper control, alongside community-level legitimacy barriers such as taboo, religious opposition, contraception myths, and normalized violence. Sustainable impact will depend on enabling implementation conditions, including reduced bureaucratic delays, stronger institutional and school support, coherent policies, reliable financing beyond donor cycles, and better data to guide targeted action.

title: Developing a systems-based programme theory for reducing night-time interactive electronic device use and improving sleep among adolescents.
authors: Rigby BP, Martin A, Shore CB, Wu X, Blake C, Haughton D, Scott H, Cleland Woods H, Evans R, Simpson SA.
abstract: Background Adolescent night-time use of interactive electronic devices (IEDs) is increasingly linked to poor sleep, mental health challenges, and reduced academic performance. However, existing interventions often overlook the complex systems shaping these behaviours. This study presents a first-of-its-kind systems-based programme theory for CLOCK OFF - a peer influence intervention aimed at reducing night-time IED use and improving adolescent sleep - created through novel participatory mapping activities and analyses, which involved adolescents, parents and teachers. Methods We conducted five online participatory workshops with adolescents (aged 11-14 years), parents, and teachers across four United Kingdom schools, supported by desk-based research. Workshop activities were facilitated using StickyStudio software. Causal loop diagramming was used to identify system components and feedback loops influencing adolescent IED use and sleep. Causal loop diagrams (CLDs) were iteratively built using Kumu software, refined and validated through stakeholder input and network analysis. The final CLD informed the development of a systems-based programme theory. Results Thirty participants (23 adolescents, 7 adults) contributed to the systems mapping process. The final CLD comprised 68 factors (i.e., causal influences of night-time IED use) and 131 connections between these factors, spanning behavioural, educational, psychological, physiological, social, and technological domains. CLOCK OFF-related mechanisms were represented across a large proportion of the system's identified feedback structures. The programme theory diagram included 72 factors and 147 feedback loops, grouped into five subsystems. These subsystems highlighted the dynamic interplay between enjoyment, overstimulation, fear of missing out (FOMO), emotional regulation, and educational stress. Conclusions Participatory systems mapping with adolescents is a feasible and valuable method for surfacing complex behavioural drivers and informing intervention design. CLOCK OFF's systems-based programme theory offers a novel approach for understanding and addressing adolescent night-time IED use and sleep disruption. Findings support the need for multi-actor and peer-led, multi-level interventions embedded within broader systemic strategies.

title: Once yearly cell-based therapy for sustained and dose-tunable delivery of monoclonal antibodies.
authors: Fell C, Davis AE, Pandey S, Guinn MT, Wang Z, DeBonis J, Smith C, Brown N, Murungi D, Kim Y, Mohandessi I, Bednarz P, Ardeshir A, Haupt EM, Cuevas SI, Lavine CL, Seaman MS, Igoshin O, Ghanta RK, Diehl MR, Veiseh O.
abstract: More than 200 monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) are approved for clinical use, yet their therapeutic potential is constrained by dependence on repeated injections or infusions that drive nonadherence, limit access in low-resource settings, and generate peak-trough pharmacokinetics linked to adverse effects and reduced efficacy. Here, we developed an immunomodulatory, encapsulated cell-based "biologics factory" that overcomes mAb instability, immunogenicity, and the fibrotic foreign body response that have limited previous approaches, enabling continuous in situ production of therapeutic antibodies from a single administration. Screening chemically modified alginate biomaterials in immunocompetent mice identified a lead immunomodulatory alginate formulation that sustains stable serum titers of the HIV-neutralizing mAb 3BNC117 for 1 year. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that this formulation promotes a local anti-inflammatory, proresolving immune niche that attenuates fibrosis. The platform's versatility was demonstrated by the production of 13 diverse mAbs from an allogeneic cell chassis, with sustained in vivo delivery of a subset including ipilimumab, pembrolizumab, adalimumab, and PGT121. Integration into a retrievable macrodevice enabled on-demand therapeutic termination and reimplantation for dose-proportional tuning. In a nonhuman primate, subcutaneous implantation maintained stable ipilimumab titers for more than 6 months with no detectable toxicity, antidrug antibodies, or adverse events, and dose-dependent exposure was confirmed across a three-dose escalation. These results demonstrate a clinically translatable platform that offers a practical strategy to replace frequent injections with single-administration therapy. A cell-based delivery platform within an antifibrotic minimally invasive device enables year-long mAb delivery.

title: Livelihoods after resettlement: women's work, collective care, and solidarity in disaster recovery.
authors: Goswami S, Parpiani M, Raju E.
abstract: This paper critically examines livelihood recovery in the peripheral resettlement sites of Chennai, India, following the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. Despite the implementation of various gender-inclusive livelihood programmes as a part of disaster recovery, our longitudinal empirical research reveals a persistent gap between formal recovery measures and the everyday conditions required for livelihoods to become gender-inclusive and sustainable over time. Drawing on in-depth fieldwork, we explore how women respond in the long term to these limitations: not simply through individual coping strategies but also by developing and maintaining collective, care-centred practices, including adapting domestic spaces to work, sharing childcare responsibilities, and building networks of mutual support. These practices are often invisible in official recovery frameworks, yet they serve as critical choices for women both to sustain their livelihoods and perform their care roles. We build on Joan C. Tronto and Berenice Fisher's (1990) theory of caring to conceptualise these acts as forms of 'caring with', where care becomes a collective, political, and relational response to systemic exclusion. In doing so, we reposition disaster recovery not merely as a return to normalcy or economic productivity but also as a deeply social and gendered process that is shaped by care and solidarity.

title: Robotic Flexible Ureteroscopy: A Step-by-Step Guide to the ILY® Platform.
authors: Marchini GS, Alves GKJ, Sepúlveda RJS, Danilovic A, Torricelli FCM, Vicentini FC, Batagello CA, Perrella R, Simões PAA, Silva AG, Nahas WC, Mazzucchi E.
journal: International braz j urol : official journal of the Brazilian Society of Urology
abstract: Introduction Robotic flexible ureteroscopy (rfURS) is emerging as an alternative to manual flexible ureteroscopy for the treatment of upper urinary tract stones. Contemporary guidelines and reviews describe its potential ergonomic and radiation-related advantages, as well as comparable surgical outcomes (1-5). Initial clinical and simulation studies with the ILY® platform have demonstrated feasibility, safety, and a short learning curve, although standardized implementation remains limited (6-10). This video presents a step-by-step workflow for the safe and efficient use of the ILY® platform. Materials and methods A 43-year-old woman with a previous right double-J stent placed for obstructive pyelonephritis underwent rfURS for a 13-mm renal pelvic stone (1,497 HU; volume 1,214 mm³). The video demonstrates operating-room setup, robot calibration and sterile draping, robot positioning and fixation, docking to the ureteral access sheath and ureteroscope assembly, console-controlled navigation, laser lithotripsy, systematic renal inspection, and standardized undocking. A flexible suction sheath was used throughout the procedure. Results Draping and docking times were 167 and 645 seconds, respectively. Robotic console time was 115 minutes, including 52 minutes of laser lithotripsy at 8 Hz and 1.2 J. Basket extraction was not required. Undocking was completed in 74 seconds, and total operative time was 130 minutes. No intraoperative complications or troubleshooting events occurred. Postoperative day-1 computed tomography confirmed stone-free status. The patient was discharged at 36 hours postoperatively without complications, as graded by the Clavien-Dindo classification (11). Surgeon satisfaction was rated 8 out of 10. Conclusion rfURS using the ILY® platform was feasible, safe, and effective. A standardized step-by-step workflow may facilitate adoption, improve procedural consistency, and enhance surgeon ergonomics (12). rfURS represents a meaningful step toward autonomous surgery (13).

title: How unequal is unequal? Turn-taking simulation for benchmarking participation and opportunity inequality in small-group collaboration.
authors: Hu L, Wu J, Yu F, Wang D, An S, Zhang Y.
abstract: Participation equity is essential for ensuring that students gain cognitive and social benefits from collaborative learning, yet there is a lack of quantitative benchmarks for interpreting participation and opportunity distributions in small-group collaboration. This study focuses on two turn-based analytical dimensions of participation equity: participation equality, measured by students' shares of speaking turns, and opportunity equality, measured by students' shares of addressed opportunities. Using the standard deviation of these rates, the study establishes preliminary, context-specific simulation-based reference values for identifying departures from an idealized triadic turn-taking baseline. The empirical dataset included 117 fourth-grade primary school students from two classes in mainland China, who worked in heterogeneous triads on mathematical and reading tasks. Using agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulation, the study estimated local turn-taking parameters from empirical data, generated reference distributions under an ideal-equity baseline, and conducted sensitivity analyses to examine model stability. Results support the internal stability of the model and provide turn-count-specific reference values for interpreting participation and opportunity inequality. The findings offer preliminary reference values for interpreting participation and opportunity distributions in collaborative learning and highlight the importance of turn count when evaluating structural patterns of participation and opportunity in triadic classroom dialogue. These reference values describe structural participation patterns rather than collaboration quality and require recalibration and independent validation before application in other educational settings.

title: Fertility in the Shadow of Cancer: Experiences of Reproductive Loss Among Women with Gynecological Cancers in Ghana.
authors: Afaya A, Amenah DB, Chambas F, Aidoo P, Gideon OA, Vidzor M, Aidoo B, Afaya RA, Avane MA, Daniels-Donkor SS, Daliri DB, Salia SM.
abstract: Background Gynecological cancers remain a threat to women's health in Ghana, where the burden is shaped by late diagnosis, limited specialized care, and treatment-related infertility. Surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy can damage the ovaries and uterus, causing premature ovarian failure, early menopause, and loss of reproductive potential. In a pronatalist context where motherhood supports identity, marriage stability, and social standing, infertility carries a psychosocial burden. Yet, the lived experiences of women with gynecological cancer-related infertility remain poorly understood. Objective This study explored the experiences of reproductive loss among women with gynecological cancers receiving care at a tertiary referral hospital in Ghana. Methods A qualitative descriptive design guided the study. Fourteen women aged 22-48 years with cervical, ovarian, uterine, or endometrial cancers, who had completed or were undergoing treatment, were purposively recruited. Semi-structured interviews (30-45 minutes) were conducted face-to-face or by telephone in private settings in English, Twi, or Ewe by trained nurses, audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed inductively using thematic analysis. Results Three interconnected themes and thirteen subthemes emerged from the data: (1) psychological and emotional experiences, (2) social challenges, and (3) coping and resilience strategies. Fertility loss was experienced as a threat to womanhood, motherhood, and relational security, especially among younger, single, and childless participants. Women undergoing active treatment emphasized symptom burden, whereas those post-treatment focused on childbearing loss. Participants described incompleteness, fear of rejection, anxiety, denial, and shattered aspirations, while social stigma and strained intimate relationships intensified distress. These experiences were compounded by treatment-related symptoms, financial strain, and interrupted education. Coping drew on adherence to treatment, dietary changes, prayer, and family support, which helped sustain hope and resilience. Conclusion Reproductive loss among women with gynecological cancers in Ghana is a psychosocial, sociocultural, and economic burden that affects quality of life. Holistic, culturally sensitive care should integrate fertility counseling, psychosocial support, symptom management, financial protection, and guidance on alternative family-building options such as adoption.

title: Recurrent Ovarian Torsion Despite Previous Oophoropexy in a 9-Year-Old Prepubertal Girl: A Pediatric Emergency Department Perspective.
authors: Alqahtani FJ.
journal: The American journal of case reports
abstract: BACKGROUND Ovarian torsion is an uncommon but time-sensitive gynecologic emergency in children. Diagnosis may be challenging because symptoms can be nonspecific and Doppler ultrasonography may demonstrate residual ovarian blood flow. Although oophoropexy may be performed to reduce recurrence, torsion can recur after fixation. CASE REPORT A 9-year-old prepubertal girl with a history of left ovarian torsion treated by laparoscopic detorsion and oophoropexy presented with 2 days of severe intermittent left-sided abdominal pain and 1 day of vomiting. She was afebrile and hemodynamically stable, without peritoneal signs. Transabdominal ultrasonography demonstrated an enlarged left ovary measuring 41×37×32 mm (approximately 27 mL), with diminished vascularity and faint internal flow on color and power Doppler imaging. Urgent laparoscopy confirmed recurrent left ovarian torsion of approximately 360°. The ovary was viable, and no ovarian cyst or adnexal mass was identified. Detorsion and utero-ovarian ligament plication were performed, preserving the ovary. At 8-week follow-up, ultrasonography demonstrated normalization of the left ovarian size to 16×14×24 mm (approximately 2.7 mL), with no adnexal lesion or pelvic free fluid. CONCLUSIONS Recurrent ovarian torsion can occur despite previous oophoropexy. Residual Doppler flow should not exclude torsion when clinical suspicion remains high. Prompt surgical evaluation can permit detorsion and ovarian preservation.

title: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology images.
authors: Wu CI, Banda K, Arora R, Soong TR, Radke M, Dillon M, Nik-Zainal S, Swisher EM, Sailem HZ.
abstract: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is a critical biomarker for guiding treatment decisions in high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), a cancer with few reliable biomarkers. However, existing genomics-based tests for HRD are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. We develop HRDPath, a patient-level deep learning architecture that predicts HRD status from whole slide images, requiring no additional molecular testing. HRDPath is validated across three cohorts of female patients and achieves an AUC of 0.846, significantly outperforming previously reported results in HGSOC. By incorporating multiple slides per patient and targeted optimization strategies, we strengthen the model clinical utility, with both specificity and sensitivity reaching 0.90. Our interpretability pipeline enhances model trustworthiness and reveals important clinical and biological insights into HRD-positive cancers, highlighting the associated morphological and pathological changes at the cellular and tissue levels. HRDPath provides a foundation for an accessible and scalable digital biomarker to improve treatment stratification in ovarian cancer globally.

title: TUBA4A Pathogenic Variant Manifesting With Adulthood-Onset Genetic Myasthenic Syndrome, Myopathy, and Infertility.
authors: Milone M, Nicolau S, Niu Z, Liewluck T, Sorenson EJ, Shen XM, Harper CM, Litchy WJ.
abstract: Objectives TUBA4A pathogenic variants are associated with ALS, frontotemporal dementia, spastic ataxia, spasticity, ataxia, Parkinson's disease, female infertility, macrothrombocytopenia, and myopathy. Four recently reported patients with TUBA4A neonatal/childhood onset myopathy had also a decrement on repetitive nerve stimulation (RNS), but such a finding was not further characterized. We describe a patient with a TUBA4A pathogenic variant with adulthood-onset genetic myasthenic syndrome accompanied by myopathy and infertility to highlight the neuromuscular junction defect as the main feature of the patient's phenotype. Methods We reviewed the patient's clinical and laboratory findings and performed transcriptomic analysis on the patient's muscle. Results A 53-year-old woman with infertility of unknown etiology manifested fatigability and proximal upper limb muscle weakness in her mid-30s, followed by lower limb involvement. Her examination showed proximal muscle weakness and fatigability but spared facial muscles. CK values were mildly elevated. Anti-AChR, MuSK, P/Q-type calcium channel, and LRP4 antibodies were absent. 2 Hz RNS showed decrement (-14% to -48%) in limb muscles that improved with 3,4-dyaminopyridine (3,4-DAP). Facilitation (231%) occurred in the trapezius. Muscle biopsy showed patchy loss of oxidative enzyme reactivity and no C5b9 or IgG at neuromuscular junctions. Whole genome sequencing identified a heterozygous known TUBA4A pathogenic variant (c.850G>A, p.Glu284Lys). Patient improved with 3,4-DAP and albuterol. Discussion TUBA4A p.Glu284Lys can lead to treatable myasthenic syndrome with postsynaptic and likely presynaptic involvement, as suggested by the patient's electrophysiological findings and response to therapy. This patient expands the TUBA4A-disorder spectrum to include overlapping myasthenic syndrome-myopathy and shows that neuromuscular disease and infertility can occur within the same patient.

authors: Das S, Yerraballa SRN, Shekhawat P.
journal: The American journal of case reports
abstract: BACKGROUND Functional neurological disorder (FND) is characterized by neurological symptoms identified through positive clinical signs that are incongruent with recognized structural neurological disease. Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS), in contrast, is defined by excessive orthostatic tachycardia and is associated with a range of multisystem autonomic symptoms. Shared clinical features can blur diagnostic boundaries. As a result, new or evolving symptoms in patients with a prior functional diagnosis may be overlooked, increasing the risk of diagnostic overshadowing. CASE REPORT An 18-year-old woman with a prior diagnosis of FND presented with fluctuating lower-extremity weakness, gait disturbance, and recurrent drop attacks. She also reported persistent orthostatic intolerance and symptom improvement with recumbency. These symptoms had previously been attributed to the functional diagnosis. Neurological examination demonstrated positive signs of functional weakness, consistent with the prior FND diagnosis. The Composite Autonomic Symptom Score (COMPASS-31) was markedly elevated. Head-up tilt table testing demonstrated sustained sinus tachycardia, with reproduction of typical orthostatic symptoms; other autonomic responses were largely preserved. Generalized joint hypermobility (Beighton score 4/9 with positive historical hypermobility) met the 2017 criteria for hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome based on family history and chronic musculoskeletal pain. Over several months, functional status improved from wheelchair dependence to independent standing, with reduced symptoms during multidisciplinary care; these findings are reported as a temporal association rather than causal inference. CONCLUSIONS This case demonstrates the coexistence of POTS in a patient with established FND and highlights the importance of systematic autonomic evaluation in individuals with persistent orthostatic symptoms. A prior functional diagnosis should not preclude investigation for coexisting physiological disorders.

abstract: Background Since 2015, oral emergency contraceptives (ECs) have been available in German community pharmacies without prescription as over-the-counter medicines. abstract: BACKGROUND Noonan syndrome is a clinically diagnosed genetic disorder frequently associated with congenital and structural cardiac abnormalities such as valvular dysplasia and cardiomyopathy, which may predispose patients to infective endocarditis. The patient improved clinically and was discharged with a plan for elective valve surgery after infection control. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights infective endocarditis as a serious complication in late-diagnosed Noonan syndrome due to underlying structural cardiac abnormalities. Early recognition of Noonan syndrome and multidisciplinary management are essential to improve outcomes and ensure timely referral for definitive cardiac intervention.

title: Social Physiology: Human homeostasis is more efficient in social proximity.

abstract: Physiological homeostasis is traditionally viewed as an individual process optimized through evolution to minimize the energetic costs of regulation. Glucose metabolism is one such system. In a set of preregistered experiments, we found that glucose homeostasis following a carbohydrate challenge is more efficient in a Social condition than an Alone condition, exhibiting lower perturbation amplitude and faster recovery ( n = 108). Evolutionarily, Social Physiology reveals a psychobiological benefit of sociality, beyond its behavioral and ecological advantages, that may contribute to the emergence and maintenance of social bonds.

abstract: Background and aims Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) is an inherited disorder of branched-chain amino acid metabolism caused by deficiency of the branched-chain α-keto acid dehydrogenase complex. Clinical examination additionally revealed bilateral pes cavus and persistent mild distal lower-limb weakness. Our findings expand the phenotypic spectrum by documenting the longitudinal evolution from recurrent childhood neurological episodes to chronic mixed demyelinating-axonal polyneuropathy. The clinical course supports the hypothesis that repeated metabolic decompensation may contribute to cumulative peripheral nerve injury. Although the precise mechanisms remain uncertain, mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired energy metabolism, oxidative stress, and branched-chain amino acid and α-keto acid toxicity provide plausible explanations. Conclusion Peripheral neuropathy should be recognized as a potential manifestation of MSUD, including intermittent phenotypes. Long-term neurological follow-up incorporating electrophysiological evaluation may improve recognition of peripheral nervous system involvement and contribute to a more complete characterization of the disease.

journal: The American journal of case reports
abstract: BACKGROUND Standard screening mammogram views focus on the lateral and posterior breast tissues; the view that best visualizes the intermammary area, the 90-degree lateral or cleavage view, is not typically performed. To date, intermammary primary breast carcinoma has been reported only a few times in the literature, and none of these described direct sternal invasion at presentation. Subsequent diagnostic workup including targeted ultrasound, and PET-CT identified a hypermetabolic presternal mass. Notably, diagnostic mammography 8 months after the initial screening mammogram also failed to properly visualize the lesion. Biopsy confirmed ER+/PR+, HER2- adenocarcinoma consistent with breast origin. Despite negative initial staging for distant metastasis, pathological examination after resection revealed direct invasion into the sternum, necessitating partial sternectomy. abstract: BACKGROUND Postsurgical pyoderma gangrenosum is a rare neutrophilic dermatosis that can mimic infection, wound dehiscence, malignancy, foreign-body reaction, or impaired surgical healing. Researchers conducted a mixed-methods study using program data collected between August 2023 and October 2024. Data included key informant interviews (n = 29) and a group discussion (n = 10). Quantitative data included village workshop records (n = 91) and household surveys and observations (n = 1,243) from 12 villages affected by floods, landslides, and drought. Researchers used descriptive statistics and logistic regression and triangulated the findings with deductive qualitative analysis informed by an implementation science framework. Results indicated that CCRIW guidance was perceived as relevant but was adapted during implementation rather than adopted as a complete stand-alone protocol. These adaptations appeared to improve short-term practicality while reducing consistent application, depth of learning, and recall of CCRIW as a distinct approach. Communities primarily adopted lower-cost actions aligned with immediate needs, available resources, and perceived feasibility. Household modifications supported more resilient and inclusive access but could not replace system-level investments under severe hazards. Regression models showed district-level associations for several facility-specific outcomes, limited associations with multiple-hazard exposure, and no consistent associations with reported household characteristics. The findings suggest that CCRIW could connect lived hazard experience with inclusive WASH assessment and local planning but should be embedded within sequenced programming that provides a WASH inclusion foundation and coordinated institutional support to address risks beyond household and village capacity.

title: Comparative analysis of host responses to Oropouche viruses in placental cell infection models.
authors: Latham KA, Brassington G, Pittman AM, Dietrich I, Hughes J, Kazungu Y, Plante JA, Plante KS, Sharp A, Brennan B, Holder B, Strang BL, Kohl A.
abstract: 2022-2024 saw a major outbreak of midge-borne Oropouche virus (OROV, Peribunyaviridae) that affected Brazil and countries across the region and was associated with a novel reassortant of this pathogen. The description of fetal deaths, microcephaly and congenital malformations in newborns led to the question whether such pathologies had previously been overlooked or are associated with novel properties of reassortant OROV, raising the question of infection and transfer across the placenta. Here we compared infection of cultured placental cell lines (BeWo and JEG-3) with an earlier OROV isolate and a Cuban isolate from 2024. Our data suggest minor, but noticeable differences between these OROV and respective host cell responses, for example relating to IFNL3. It remains to be investigated whether characteristics of these different isolates translate to effects on fetal development, but these findings suggest that cellular responses can differ between ancestral and recent isolates of this virus.

title: Primary Care Recognition of Rabson-Mendenhall Syndrome Despite Absence of Classical Diabetic Symptoms.
authors: Al Eisa A, Aldayhani AH.
journal: The American journal of case reports
abstract: BACKGROUND Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome (RMS) is an extremely rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the insulin receptor gene, leading to severe insulin resistance and compensatory hyperinsulinemia. Classical features include acanthosis nigricans, non-obese or underweight body habitus, hirsutism, dental abnormalities, dysmorphic features, and variable growth abnormalities. Early recognition may be difficult when the initial presentation is dominated by non-specific symptoms rather than classical metabolic complaints. CASE REPORT A 10-year-old Saudi girl presented to a family medicine clinic with intermittent bilateral leg pain and excessive hunger, without polyuria or polydipsia. Examination revealed extensive acanthosis nigricans, moderate hirsutism, deep voice, high-arched palate, and dental enamel defects. Laboratory evaluation showed severe hyperinsulinemia with insulin level of 3522.5 µU/mL, elevated HbA1c of 8.4% (68 mmol/mol), and biochemical hyperandrogenism. Although RMS is classically associated with growth restriction, the patient was tall for age and had a family history of tall stature, requiring cautious interpretation of growth-related findings. Whole-exome sequencing confirmed a homozygous pathogenic insulin receptor variant (c.433C>T, p.Arg145Cys), establishing the diagnosis of RMS. Treatment included vitamin D supplementation, metformin, basal-bolus insulin therapy, dapagliflozin, home glucose monitoring, diabetes education, dietary counseling, and multidisciplinary follow-up. Glycemic control remained suboptimal despite treatment intensification, reflecting the severe receptor-level insulin resistance associated with RMS. CONCLUSIONS In this patient, marked acanthosis nigricans, severe hyperinsulinemia, hyperglycemia, and hyperandrogenic features supported evaluation for a genetic insulin resistance syndrome despite the absence of classical diabetic symptoms.

abstract: Objectives to report the care provided by nurses in the transportation module of the Cegonha Carioca Program, establishing connections with the Three Delays Model. Methods experience report describing the care delivered by nurses to pregnant and postpartum women from 2012 to 2024, based on lived experience, public data, and the scientific literature. Results public awareness of the ambulance service, along with the quality and humanization of care, aligns with reducing the delay in seeking care; Free access to the service, the strategic location of ambulances, and the presence of a designated referral maternity hospital facilitate the identification of and access to health services; Efficient communication, prioritization of care, and alert systems support timely and appropriate care. Conclusions care provided in the ambulance is grounded in a humanized model and includes actions aimed at preventing delays. journal: Revista da Escola de Enfermagem da U S P
abstract: Objective To report the use of Instructional Therapeutic Play during the preoperative nursing consultation of a child with an orofacial cleft. Method A case study conducted at an association that supports children with orofacial clefts located in northwestern Paraná, Brazil. Data were collected in May 2025 during a nursing consultation using Instructional Therapeutic Play, book reading, and drawing activities to prepare the child for surgery. The consultation was audio-and video-recorded with consent, and the data were analyzed descriptively. The study was approved by the Research Ethics Committee under Opinion 7,041,250/2024. Results The study included an 8-year-old girl scheduled to undergo cleft palate repair surgery. She presented fear and anxiety related to the surgical procedure, particularly fear of not waking up after anesthesia. The use of Instructional Therapeutic Play enabled the child to understand the procedure, express her concerns, and, at the end of the session, she reported feeling calmer. Conclusion Instructional Therapeutic Play promoted emotional expression and facilitated the surgical preparation of the child with an orofacial cleft.

title: Estimated incidence and number of new cases with prenatal alcohol exposure and fetal alcohol spectrum disorders in Finland 1990-2025.
authors: Jolma M, Koivu-Jolma M, Gissler M, Sarajuuri A, Autti-Rämö I.
abstract: Background Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD) arising from prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) are the leading preventable cause of neurobehavioral disorders. Early pregnancy is particularly vulnerable to ethanol toxicity, yet alcohol use often continues until pregnancy recognition. In Finland, national incidence estimates of PAE and FASD remain limited. Objective To estimate the incidence of any PAE and heavy PAE in Finland between 1990 and 2025, and to model the annual number of children with FASD born in Finland. Methods We developed a mathematical modelling framework integrating studies on alcohol use during pregnancy in Finland, biomarker-based estimates of heavy PAE, national population statistics, and international active case ascertainment studies on FASD prevalence. Incidence of any PAE was estimated from self-reported alcohol use, including pre-recognition exposure. Heavy PAE was estimated by combining binge-drinking prevalence, delayed pregnancy recognition, biomarker data and anonymous self-reports. FASD incidence was modelled using two approaches: 1) an international multiplier linking FASD prevalence to heavy episodic drinking prevalence among women (Model M), and 2) a conventional epidemiological ratio between any PAE and FASD (Model L). Results Self-reported alcohol use during pregnancy declined following abstinence recommendations in the early 2000s, while pre-recognition use remained relatively stable. Heavy PAE decreased from 9% (uncertainty range 7-11%) in the 1990s to 6% (4-8%) in the early 2020s. Any PAE declined from 75% (60-85%) to 32% (26-38%). Modelled FASD incidence showed similar decreasing trends, ranging from 6.8% to 5.6% (Model M), and from 6% to 3% (Model L). Conclusion PAE remains common in Finland, and the burden of FASD is substantial despite declining trends. Additional biomarker-based studies of PAE and active case ascertainment of FASD are needed to refine current estimates. Strengthened public health efforts to reduce PAE, including the efforts before recognition of pregnancy, are essential.
